hints: Look closely at the four Km numbers and ask yourself, which one is the biggest value? Remember Km is a concentration.
Recall how Km relates to affinity: a small Km means half Vmax is reached with very little substrate, so think about what a large Km tells you.
walkthrough:
**Remember what Km really means**

Think of Km as the substrate concentration needed to get the enzyme working at half its maximum rate. It is measured in $mol\ dm^{-3}$.

$$K_m = [S] \text{ when } v = \frac{V_{max}}{2}$$

**Link Km to affinity**

Affinity means how strongly and easily the enzyme grabs its substrate. High affinity means it grabs well even when there is very little substrate around.

So the rule is simple and opposite: low Km = high affinity, high Km = low affinity.

**Pick the largest Km for lowest affinity**

We need lowest affinity, so we need the highest Km. Compare the powers of 10 first.

$$4 \times 10^{-3} > 1 \times 10^{-3} > 2 \times 10^{-4} > 1 \times 10^{-4}$$

Option A has the largest Km, so the enzyme needs the most substrate to reach half Vmax. That is the lowest affinity.

options.A: Correct. Km = 4 x 10^-3 is the largest Km, so the most substrate is needed for half Vmax, showing the lowest affinity.
options.B: Smaller Km than A, so affinity is higher than for A. It needs less substrate to reach half Vmax.
options.C: Much smaller Km (10^-4 range), so affinity is much higher than for A. A common mix-up is thinking small Km means low affinity.
options.D: Smallest Km of all, so this shows the highest affinity, the exact opposite of what the question asks for.
